Amending lands on the review page, and every page of an amendment shows an 'Amend' status bar with a 'Cancel amend' button. Copy as new keeps and clears exactly what Design Release 2.1 lists, copies the submitted version of an amendment, and returns a stale copy to where the trader started. The delete confirmation page gets a summary of the notification and new wording. After a delete, the trader lands on the overall dashboard and the notification list then says '<reference> has been deleted'.
summaries.today: Amend has no confirmation and lands on the Overview hub. Cancel amendment is a separate page with its own wording and a success banner afterwards. A copy shows counts, identification, arrival, transport and contact address as Complete, even though the record clears some of those answers. A stale Copy as new from the view page goes to an address that no route serves. The 'Delete this notification?' page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons, and after a delete the trader lands on the live-animals dashboard with 'The notification has been deleted.'

summaries.headline: Traders sign in to a new overall dashboard that summarises each kind of notification, drill down to what needs action, and manage their live animals notifications on one list with tabs, real search, filters and paging. They see only their own organisation's notifications.
summaries.whatChanges: The INS front door's home stops being a table of notifications. It becomes the Design Release 2.1 dashboard, with one section per category and glance cards that link to drill-down pages. The live animals notification list moves from the animals frontend to the INS frontend and only shows the signed-in organisation's notifications. The list gets the new cards, tabs, one search-and-sort form, additional filters and numbered pages of 8. Action needed means a submitted notification that is still missing a required document. The animals backend works this out and carries it into the INS read model.
summaries.today: Today the INS home is a page headed 'Dashboard'. It has a reference search, a sort form and a table of every notification, the same for every organisation, and search only matches a whole reference number. The live animals list lives in the animals frontend. It has a 'Filter notifications' aside, a separate 'Update sort' button, 25 cards a page with only Previous and Next links, and page titles that use a pipe with no GOV.UK suffix.

summaries.headline: Traders choose what they are importing before a notification exists, and can save, reuse, change and delete their own notification templates from a new Templates item in the navigation.
summaries.whatChanges: Starting a notification from the dashboard now asks 'What are you importing?' first. Live animals goes on to the animals journey and the plants types go on to the high-risk plants journey. A new Manage templates page lets a trader create a template by walking the same question pages in template mode, then save, view, change, use, sort, discard and delete it. Templates are stored by the backend and belong only to the user who saved them, and the journey pages learn to return to the template's review when a trader edits it from there.
summaries.today: Today the dashboard's create button goes straight into the live-animals journey and lands on the origin page with no type question, and the INS home offers 'Start a new notification' only when the trader has no notifications. No real service has notification templates, and a task page's Back link always goes to the overview, whatever it was opened from.
